location.section: 5.11 What iteration 5 established, what it ruled out, and what it abandoned

old_text: - *The movability half: the base repertoire predicts which tasks a nudge moves.* Spearman -0.03 in panel A, 0.21 in panel B and 0.15 pooled over 13 new units, below the disconfirming bound of 0.3; 4 of 10 new units diverse in the base never moved, and in panel A the runtime merit gap and the twin modal share tracked movability better than beta.
new_text: - *The movability half: the base repertoire predicts which tasks a nudge moves.* Not supported as a strong predictor, and not disconfirmed: beta is not a strong predictor of movability (Spearman 0.15 over 13 new units, Bonett-Wright 95% [-0.44, 0.65], bootstrap BCa [-0.50, 0.70], one-sided permutation p 0.317; power of the registered one-sided permutation test about 0.63 at a true 0.6, 0.50 two-sided, and 20 units for 0.8); a moderate relation is not excluded at this n; bf16-conditional. The pooled value rests on count inversions' beta of 0.75, which the panel committed on the attempt basis because only a few base programs were correct (67% of its attempts are unlabelled 'other'); on the correct-only basis used for the other twelve units its beta is 0.13 and the pooled Spearman is 0.035. Per panel Spearman -0.03 (A) and 0.21 (B); 4 of 10 new units diverse in the base never moved. Under one definition of each rival, pooled over the 13 units with signs fixed so that the predicted direction is positive: R1 0.08 (Holm p 1.000, delta +0.07 [-0.66, 0.88]); R4 -0.50 (Holm p 1.000, delta +0.65 [-0.06, 1.34]); R6 0.71 (Holm p 0.021, delta -0.57 [-1.26, 0.20]); R7 0.41 (Holm p 0.347, delta -0.26 [-1.05, 0.56]); K -0.21 (Holm p 1.000, delta +0.35 [-0.57, 1.24]). Under Holm only R6 (runtime merit) tracks movability, while beta does not; the paired interval for beta minus that rival still includes 0 (iteration-6 correction; tables/rival_scores.csv).
